```{r}
#| label: settings
#| echo: true

# ---- CHANGE THESE FOR EACH POPULATION ----------------------

pop_name <- "Exponential (rate = 1)"      # name used in the text

# Random generator: a function that takes n and returns n draws.
# Put any extra settings (rate, shape, mean, ...) inside it.
rng <- function(n) rexp(n, rate = 1)

pop_mean <- 1                             # true population mean
pop_sd   <- 1                             # true population standard deviation

sample_sizes <- c(2, 5, 10, 30, 50, 100)  # sample sizes to test
B        <- 10000                         # repeats per sample size
seed     <- 2026                          # seed reused for every n

final_n  <- NA                            # fill in after looking at results

# ------------------------------------------------------------
```

```{r}
#| label: load-functions
#| echo: true

# Load simulate_means(), summarize_means() and plot_means()
source("clt_functions.R")
```

## Which sample sizes and why

<!--
Explain why you picked these sample sizes, e.g. a few very small
ones to see the non-normal behaviour, the common "n = 30" rule
of thumb, and larger ones to confirm.
-->

The sample sizes tested were n = `r paste(sample_sizes, collapse = ", ")`,
each with B = `r format(B, big.mark = ",")` repeats.

WRITE HERE.

```{r}
#| label: simulate
#| echo: true

# Empty list to keep the sample means for each n (used for plots)
all_means <- list()

# Empty list to keep one summary row for each n
summary_rows <- list()

for (i in seq_along(sample_sizes)) {
  n <- sample_sizes[i]                    # current sample size

  set.seed(seed)                          # reset the seed for this n

  m <- simulate_means(rng, n = n, B = B)  # B sample means of size n

  all_means[[i]] <- m                     # save the means
  summary_rows[[i]] <- summarize_means(m, mu = pop_mean,
                                       sigma = pop_sd, n = n)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: results-table
#| echo: true

# Stack the one-row summaries into one table
results <- do.call(rbind, summary_rows)

# Round to 4 decimal places so the table is easy to read
shown <- round(results, 4)

# Keep 3 significant figures for the p-value instead, so very
# small p-values show as e.g. 2.5e-13 rather than 0
shown$shapiro_p <- signif(results$shapiro_p, 3)

print(shown, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: plots
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4

# One histogram + Q-Q plot pair for each sample size
for (i in seq_along(sample_sizes)) {
  plot_means(all_means[[i]], mu = pop_mean, sigma = pop_sd,
             n = sample_sizes[i],
             main = paste0(pop_name, ", n = ", sample_sizes[i]))
}
```
